subject: Notice: Deprecation of EdgeHandlers & onboarding plan for EdgeFlow (subprocessor change)
messages:
From: Jason Cole <jason.cole@finteq.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Oct 2027 08:12:00 +0000
Subject: Important: EdgeHandlers EOL and EdgeFlow transition (subprocessor update)

Hi Jonas,

Quick heads-up from Finteq procurement: we are deprecating our current log/edge routing partner 'EdgeHandlers' on 2027-11-20 and will route telemetry and asynchronous logs to a new partner, 'EdgeFlow Ltd' (edgeflow.io). EdgeFlow will handle log enrichment, real-time routing, and optional retention for troubleshooting.

Why this matters for Redwood: Finteq's contract amendments require any downstream processors that touch EU-customer-identifiable logs to be named and DPA amendments executed. EdgeFlow will host in the UK and EU regions but will also maintain a US backup failover for disaster recovery.

Attached is the EdgeFlow onboarding annex and a high-level dataflow diagram. EdgeFlow has provided a draft subprocessor annex and a SOC 2 Type II cover note. Key technical points they flagged:
- Ingest: encrypted HTTPS push from Finteq's collectors
- Storage: encrypted at rest with customer-specific KMS keys (EdgeFlow supports customer-supplied KMS via bring-your-key API)
- Processing: IP deterministic pseudonymization for certain fields (optional)
- Cross-border: asynchronous failover egress to us-east for disaster recovery only; logs will be accessible to support on request

Finteq asked us to confirm whether Redwood requires any contractual changes (DPA amendment, export controls, dataflow attestations) or additional evidence. Can you advise by EOD 2027-10-07? Procurement is on a tight schedule for their vendor cut-over.

Thanks,
Jason
Jason Cole
Vendor Relations | Finteq Payments
procurement@finteq.com

Attachments:

Subject: Fwd: Important: EdgeHandlers EOL and EdgeFlow transition (subprocessor update)

Forwarding Finteq's notice — they want confirmation on DPA/attestation items.

Kimberly / Monica,
Can you triage the annex and the dataflow diagram? Initial asks we should cover:
- Does EdgeFlow's failover to the US create a cross-border transfer that requires specific contractual language for EU residents?
- Is customer-supplied KMS (BYOK) acceptable for our existing integration model, and what evidence do we need to confirm it?
- Can we accept the proposed pseudonymization approach, or do we need stronger minimization language?

Procurement needs a short answer by 2027-10-07; I think we can ask for a 1-week extension from Finteq if needed. Markus, tagging you for any operational concerns (latency, routing) that might affect our SLAs.

Cheers,
Jonas Weber
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Fwd: Important: EdgeHandlers EOL and EdgeFlow transition (subprocessor update)

Thanks for the ping. I reviewed the annex and diagram — high level thoughts:

1) Cross-border transfers: EdgeFlow's description (EU primary + US failover) triggers an Article 46-style permitted transfer analysis for EU customers. Practically, we need:
   - A written statement from EdgeFlow that the US failover is for DR only and access is restricted to named support staff; and
   - Either SCCs between EdgeFlow and Finteq/Redwood or a DPA clause confirming appropriate safeguards.

2) BYOK: positive from a controls perspective — on paper it's good. We need technical confirmation of key wrap & KMS footprint (who holds root KMS, key rotation, and deletion guarantees). Recommend we request a short KMS FAQ from EdgeFlow and a proof-of-concept key rotation event in a staging account.

3) Pseudonymization: the annex's approach looks configurable, which is acceptable. We should require that any reversible mappings are explicitly documented and that EdgeFlow implements strict access control and audit logging for mapping keys.

4) Evidence: ask for recent SOC 2 Type II report and a network/dataflow diagram with ingress/egress IP ranges, plus a written attestation on backup egress procedures.

5) Contract language: propose a minimal DPA amendment that: lists EdgeFlow as subprocessors, restricts US failover use to DR, requires KMS controls and audit rights, and adds 30 days' notice for future subprocessor changes.

I can draft suggested DPA amendment language (short paragraph) by EOD tomorrow if you want. Monica — any concerns from engineering on routing or performance SLA impacts? Markus — any thoughts on runbook changes for incident response if logs land on EdgeFlow?

-Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
From: EdgeFlow Legal <legal@edgeflow.io>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Jason Cole <jason.cole@finteq.com>
Cc: procurement@finteq.com
Date: Tue, 12 Oct 2027 14:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Important: EdgeHandlers EOL and EdgeFlow transition (subprocessor update)

Hi all,

Thanks for the diligence and useful questions. A few clarifications to address Kimberly's points:

- US failover: confirmed DR-only. Access to US-hosted backups is restricted to named on-call engineers and only after an incident declaration; access is logged and requires manager approval. We will provide a short attestation letter and update the annex.
- KMS: EdgeFlow supports customer-supplied KMS via our BYOK API. We will provide a KMS FAQ and can perform a scheduled key-rotation event in a sandbox for Finteq and Redwood.
- Pseudonymization: we will deliver a technical note on reversible mappings and will enable a strict RBAC policy and immutable audit trail for any key/mapping operations.
- Evidence: SOC 2 Type II report is attached (redacted) and we can add IP ranges and egress procedures to the dataflow diagram.

We are amenable to the proposed DPA amendment language. To make progress, we've created a draft amendment in DocuSign (link below) that lists EdgeFlow as a subprocessor, includes the DR-only clause for US failover, and includes a BYOK/KMS annex. Please review and leave comments in DocuSign.
